claims.text: First: read the densities Denser = whiter: metal is white, bone cortex less white, muscle and fluid gray, fat darker gray, and air or gas black
claims.quote: The range of densities, from most to least dense, is represented by metal (white, or radiopaque), bone cortex (less white), muscle and fluid (gray), fat (darker gray), and air or gas (black, or radiolucent).

claims.text: In the neck, the airway shows as black air shadows: the pharyngeal air spaces and, below the larynx, the subglottic tracheal air shadow
claims.quote: Soft-tissue neck radiograph of a child with croup shows luminal narrowing of the subglottic tracheal air shadow (arrows) and dilation of the pharyngeal air spaces.
claims.locator: Diagnosis, Radiograph of a Child With Croup (Sagittal View) (image caption)

claims.text: Views and technique Get both views: AP and lateral radiographs of the neck and chest when croup is suspected but the diagnosis is uncertain
claims.quote: If there is diagnostic uncertainty, patients should have AP and lateral radiographs of the neck and chest

claims.text: Take the lateral right: during inspiration, with the neck extended and no rotation, to avoid false-positive results
claims.quote: they are not highly accurate (1) and must be taken during inspiration, during neck extension, and with no rotation to avoid false-positive results.

claims.text: What to look at AP view, below the larynx: gradual narrowing of the subglottic air column (steeple sign) = croup
claims.quote: Soft-tissue neck radiograph of a child with croup shows gradual narrowing of the subglottic tracheal lumen and its air shadow (steeple sign—arrows) and dilation of the pharyngeal air spaces.
claims.locator: Diagnosis, Radiograph of a Child With Croup (Coronal View) (image caption)

claims.text: Lateral view, the epiglottis: an enlarged epiglottis (thumb sign) with a distended hypopharynx = epiglottitis
claims.quote: Enlarged epiglottis (thumb sign) and distention of the hypopharynx

claims.text: Cautions Not the final word: neck films may help but are not highly accurate for epiglottitis
claims.quote: Although plain radiographs may be helpful, they are not highly accurate

claims.text: Epiglottitis is diagnosed by direct visualization of the supraglottic structures, only where full respiratory support is available
claims.quote: Diagnosis requires direct visualization of the supraglottic structures; this procedure is not to be performed until full respiratory support is available.

claims.text: Airway first: imaging should not delay management in an unstable patient, and a child with stridor should not be sent to the x-ray suite
claims.quote: Lateral neck radiography should not delay definitive management in unstable patients. For example, a child with stridor should not be transported to the x-ray suite due to risk of a life-threatening decompensation and airway collapse either en route or during such positioning.
